payload.prompt: Enviámos uma fatura de 10765 EUR ao Estrela Lda (org. nº 950948086) quando a taxa de câmbio era 11.30 NOK/EUR. O cliente pagou agora, mas a taxa é 10.78 NOK/EUR. Registe o pagamento e lance a diferença cambial (disagio) na conta correta.

payload.goal: Register payment for invoice of 10765 EUR issued to Estrela Lda, accounting for the exchange rate difference (disagio) between invoice rate (11.30 NOK/EUR) and payment rate (10.78 NOK/EUR), posting the FX loss to the correct account.
likely_resources: Account for FX loss (disagio): typically account 8160 (Valutatap) in Norwegian chart of accounts
success_checks: Invoice of 10765 EUR is marked as paid in Tripletex
Payment registered at rate 10.78 NOK/EUR (116,046.70 NOK received)
FX loss of 5,597.80 NOK posted to account 8160 (Valutatap/disagio)
Accounts receivable (1500) cleared fully (no residual balance on invoice)
Voucher created with correct debit/credit entries for FX difference
Bank account reflects actual NOK amount received (116,046.70 NOK)
risk_notes: Invoice currency is EUR but bank account may be NOK — confirm bank account currency before registering payment
Tripletex may not automatically split FX difference; a manual journal voucher (bilagsføring) may be required for the disagio entry
Account 8160 (Valutatap) is standard for FX loss in Norway — confirm with client's chart of accounts if customized
If invoice was booked at 11.30, AR balance is 121,644.50 NOK; payment clears 116,046.70 NOK, leaving 5,597.80 NOK open — this residual must be manually written off to 8160
Ensure the customer Estrela Lda exists in Tripletex; org. number 950948086 appears to be a Portuguese NIF — verify it is correctly registered
VAT treatment on FX loss posting: FX differences are typically VAT-exempt (account 8160 has no VAT)
If the invoice was already sent and posted, do not delete or reverse it — only register payment and post the difference
payload.suggested_first_action: Look up or create customer Estrela Lda (org. 950948086) and locate the open EUR invoice for 10765 EUR in Tripletex to confirm its posted NOK value at 11.30 rate.

line_items.description: Fatura original — 10765 EUR ao câmbio 11.30 NOK/EUR
Diferença cambial (disagio) — perda de câmbio conta 8160 Valutatap

ordered_steps: 1. Verify customer Estrela Lda (org. 950948086) exists via GET /customer — create if missing via POST /customer
2. Locate the open EUR invoice for 10765 EUR via GET /invoice?customerId={id}&currency=EUR — confirm posted NOK value = 121,644.50 NOK at rate 11.30
3. Register payment on the invoice via POST /invoice/{id}/payment with amount 116,046.70 NOK (10765 EUR × 10.78), payment date = today, bank account = NOK account
4. Note the residual open balance of 5,597.80 NOK on the invoice (AR not fully cleared)
5. Create a manual journal voucher via POST /ledger/voucher to post the FX loss:
- VAT code: exempt (no VAT on FX difference)
6. Verify invoice is fully cleared (balance = 0) via GET /invoice/{id}
7. Verify account 8160 has the disagio entry via GET /ledger/account/8160/balance
8. Confirm bank account reflects 116,046.70 NOK received

rules: Use params={"number": XXXX} to resolve a specific account number to its ID.
This is a QUERY PARAM via the params field — NOT json_body.
Do NOT use /ledger/accountingPeriod — it does not exist.
For bank account setup: isBankAccount=true, bankAccountNumber='12345678903', bankAccountCountry={"id": 161}.
MUST include id and version from the GET response.
When email is provided, ALWAYS set BOTH email AND invoiceEmail to the same value.
Do NOT send isCustomer (it's readOnly and auto-set).
For addresses, use postalAddress={addressLine1, postalCode, city, country={id: 161}} for Norway.
ALWAYS search first if product_number is provided: GET /product?number=<number> — sandbox pre-seeds products.
Only POST /product if GET returns 0 results.
Use 'number' field for the product number (NOT productNumber).
priceExcludingVat sets the base price. Also set vatType={"id": 3|5|6}.
Requires customer={"id": customer_id}.
Set orderDate and deliveryDate (use today_iso from execution_brief).
When a product was created, ALWAYS include product={"id": product_id} on the orderline.
Use unitPriceExcludingVatCurrency for the price field.
Set vatType={"id": 3} for 25%, {"id": 5} for 15%, {"id": 6} for 0%.
For multiple lines, prefer POST /order/orderline/list for efficiency.
Pass orders=[{"id": order_id}] to link order.
Set invoiceDate and invoiceDueDate.
Bank account 1920 MUST be configured first (see bank account setup pattern).
Method is PUT, not POST.
ALL params are QUERY PARAMETERS — NOT in body: PUT /invoice/{id}/:payment?paymentDate=YYYY-MM-DD&paymentTypeId=XXXXX&paidAmount=YYYYY
Do NOT send a JSON body — send empty body or no body. ALL data goes in the URL query string.
Get paymentTypeId first via GET /invoice/paymentType — use the first result's id.
paidAmount is the full payment amount (e.g., 47200). For foreign currency, use paidAmountCurrency instead.
REQUIRES dateFrom and dateTo as query params. Without them you get 422.
dateTo is EXCLUSIVE — if you want vouchers from March 22, use dateTo=2026-03-23 (next day).
NEVER use dateFrom == dateTo — it always returns 422. Always set dateTo = dateFrom + 1 day minimum.
Example for single day: params={"dateFrom": "2026-03-22", "dateTo": "2026-03-23"}
Example for broad range: params={"dateFrom": "2026-01-01", "dateTo": "2026-12-31"}
These are QUERY PARAMS via the params field — NOT json_body.
Method is PUT, not POST.
date is a QUERY PARAMETER: PUT /ledger/voucher/{id}/:reverse?date=YYYY-MM-DD
Do NOT send date in the request body.
ALWAYS set BOTH amountGross AND amountGrossCurrency to the SAME value on every posting.
Do NOT include postings with row=0 — row 0 is system-generated and will cause a 422.
AUTO-SPLIT RULES: ONLY vatType id=3 (25% utgående) triggers auto-split. vatType id=1 does NOT auto-split.
For supplier costs: use vatType=3 (NOT id=1) with ONLY the debit posting. Tripletex detects the expense account and applies inngående MVA automatically.
For vatType=0: include BOTH debit AND credit postings manually. They must sum to 0.
If you get 422 'postings don't sum to 0': switch to vatType=3 with single debit posting, OR add both debit+credit with vatType=0.
NEVER use vatType=1 — it does NOT auto-generate balancing entries and will always cause 422 with single posting.
Do NOT include currency on postings — let it default. Including currency={} causes 'factor must be >= 1' error.
For supplier invoices, set supplier={"id": supplier_id} on the debit posting.
Resolve account numbers: GET /ledger/account with params={"number": XXXX}, then use account={"id": resolved_id}. NEVER use account={"number": XXXX} in postings.

I'm reconsidering the approach: create the invoice in EUR, register payment using paidAmountCurrency for the full EUR amount to mark it as paid, and then potentially create a separate voucher for the FX difference if Tripletex doesn't handle it automatically when payments come in at different rates.

The real challenge is that in the sandbox, I can't control what exchange rate Tripletex uses when creating the EUR invoice—it'll use its current rate rather than the historical 11.30 NOK/EUR rate specified in the task, so there may be a mismatch I need to account for.

My approach: create the invoice in EUR for 10765, register payment for the full EUR amount, then create a separate journal voucher to record the FX loss (disagio) by debiting the currency loss account and crediting accounts receivable for 5597.80 NOK. Since the voucher needs both debit and credit postings with vatType=0, I'll structure it that way.

Now I need to resolve the account references and plan out the API sequence: first verify or create the necessary ledger accounts (1920 for the bank, 8160 for currency losses, and 1500 for receivables), then create the order with EUR currency and the invoice line, post the invoice, register the payment, and finally create the journal voucher for the FX difference.

First voucher POST failed with 422 'Kunde mangler' because the 1500 (Kundefordringer) posting lacked a customer reference, requiring a retry and wasting one API call.

The disagio voucher may have used wrong amount precision or account direction causing Check 3 to fail even after the retry succeeded (e.g., amountGrossCurrency should be 0 for NOK-only postings, not 5597.8).

FX loss calculation (5,597.80 NOK) and account selection (8160 debit, 1500 credit) were logically correct.

Review what Check 3 specifically validates (possibly the payment paidAmount vs paidAmountCurrency fields or the voucher posting structure) and ensure the disagio voucher postings balance correctly with proper currency fields.
